title: Achieving abstraction with an abstract class
answer: Yes. An abstract class alone can provide abstraction by declaring one or more abstract operations and exposing concrete behavior that depends on them. Callers can use the abstract base type while subclasses provide the hidden implementation. Interfaces are another abstraction mechanism, but they are not mandatory when a single stateful class hierarchy is the right design.
